app.sin_conexion: No connection to the simulator. Retrying…
averia.detalle: Since {inicio}. It will be repaired automatically at {fin} (simulated time), at the current speed (×{acelerar}).
averia.reparar_ayuda: Ends the breakdown right now, with its end event and its maintenance report.
conf.subtitulo: What is sent and where. None of this stops the simulation: it only changes what comes out of it.
conf.equipos_ayuda: Turn a piece of equipment off to stop sending its data. It is still simulated: when you turn it back on, its values carry on from where they were.
conf.salidas_ayuda: Where the data is sent. Turning an output off does not stop the simulation: it just stops writing or publishing to it.
conf.dato_sucio_activar: Add dirty data to what is sent
conf.dato_sucio_ayuda: Deliberately spoils a small part of the telemetry and events, to practise cleaning: null or absurd values, duplicated messages, dates in another format, counters that reset to zero and gripper bounces. The simulation does not change, only what is sent. What you see on this page is always the clean data, except in “What is being sent”.
conf.mensajes_ayuda: The latest messages as they go out to the files and MQTT (with dirty data, if enabled). Most recent first. The ts field is in UTC; the page header, in local time.
salida.jsonl_equipo: JSON Lines files, one per day, in {ruta}/<line>/<equipment>/<channel>/: telemetry, events, inspections, orders and texts. This is what Logstash or Python read from file.
salida.jsonl_canal: JSON Lines files, one per day, in {ruta}/<channel>/: telemetry, events, inspections, orders and texts. This is what Logstash or Python read from file.
salida.curva_csv: Quarter-hourly load curve of the main meter in {ruta}/, as a Spanish-style CSV (with ; and decimal comma), like the one the distribution company provides.
salida.logs: One text log per piece of equipment in {ruta}/, with a different format depending on the equipment type, like those of real controllers.
salida.mqtt: Publishes every message to the MQTT broker, on topics {prefijo}/<line>/<equipment>/<channel> (e.g. {prefijo}/L1/cnc-01/telemetria). This is what Node-RED and Python read live.
inc.ayuda: To see in the data what happens when something fails.
inc.averia_ayuda: The equipment breaks down and stops the line: the PLC and the equipment go to AVERIA and the rest to ESPERA. It generates the start and end events, a line in the equipment log and, once repaired, a maintenance report. If it happens off shift, the line stays stopped when it ends.
inc.microparada_ayuda: A short stop with a warning alarm (code W-…): the line goes to MICROPARADA and then resumes production. It only works while the line is producing.
inc.fuga_aire_ayuda: Increases air consumption: the compressor spends more time loaded and uses more energy, and pressure may drop below the minimum (alarm W-410). It lasts until you remove it. It does not use the duration.
inc.fallo_inversor_ayuda: The photovoltaic system stops generating for the given minutes (state FALLO): the plant buys more energy from the grid. At night it is hardly noticeable.
acceso.output: In Output, choose “a parsed JSON object”: the data arrives in msg.payload.
acceso.ninguna: None of the readable outputs is configured.
ficha.dibujo_ayuda: Illustrative animation: it moves according to the real state and cycles of the equipment, a few seconds behind the simulation (so that it only draws what has already happened). The state at the top and the telemetry are up to the moment.
ficha.tendencia_ayuda: Up to the last 30 simulated minutes, since the simulator started; choose up to 3 fields. Hover (or drag a finger) over it to see the values, or view it as a table. The full history is in the files.
ficha.valores_ayuda: Latest message, with the field names exactly as they appear in the data.
ficha.sin_telemetria: The first sample has not arrived yet.
ficha.sin_telemetria_mes: The MES does not publish telemetry: it publishes one message per production order when it closes.
ficha.sin_eventos: No events since the simulator started.
ficha.sin_inspecciones: No part has been inspected yet.
ficha.sin_ordenes: No order has been closed yet.
dest.calculado_web: Calculated by the web page (not in the data)
prob.degradacion: Predicted failure: {variable} is {pct} % above normal (failure at {limite} %)
portada.sinoptico_aria: Animated diagram of the plant and its equipment
portada.ayuda_sinoptico: Click a piece of equipment to see its page. The animation is illustrative: it moves with the real state and cycles, a few seconds behind the simulation so that it only draws what has already happened. The parts on the conveyor represent the flow; the simulator does not give their position.
portada.modo_rapido: Fast mode (×{x}): the process is shown with representative cycles, slower than the real ones so it can be followed. States, breakdowns and values are the real ones.
portada.oee_pie: Calculated by the web page: availability × performance × quality
oee.pocos_datos: The shift has just started: with so few pieces, the OEE still swings a lot.
portada.avisos_ayuda: Alarms, breakdowns and notable changes since the simulator started.
portada.desliza: Swipe the diagram sideways to see the whole plant.
portada.paso1: Loading: robot-01 picks the raw part from the conveyor and places it on the CNC loading pallet.
portada.paso2: Machining: when the previous part is finished, the pallets swap; the CNC machines the part and it comes out onto the conveyor.
portada.paso3: Welding: robot-02 welds the machined part.
portada.paso4: Quality: its dimensions are measured; good parts go to the box and bad ones to the reject bin.
prod.subtitulo: How each line is doing: state, production order, shift OEE and part quality.
prod.orden_ayuda: Progress is calculated by the web page: orders are only published when they close.
prod.sin_turno: No shift has started since the simulator started.
prod.cronologia_ayuda: Hover over a segment to see times and reason.
prod.cuenta_disp: Time producing ({prod}) divided by planned time ({plan}): the shift without breaks or preventive maintenance.
prod.cuenta_rend: Parts made ({piezas}) divided by the theoretical ones at the nominal rate, one every {s} s while producing ({teoricas}).
prod.cuenta_cal: Good parts ({ok}) divided by parts made ({total}).
prod.tiempo_estados: Time in each state during the shift
prod.oee_nota: This is an approximate calculation by this web page: the OEE is not in the data the simulator publishes. Start-ups and changeovers count as lost time.
prod.ultimas_n: In the last {n} inspected parts there are {nok} NOK ({pct} %).
prod.nok_ayuda: Machining dimensions (diameter, length) fail when the CNC tool is worn; welding ones, when the welding robot degrades.
prod.ordenes_ayuda: Click an order to see its materials: planned, actually consumed, and batches.
ener.subtitulo: Where the plant's energy comes from, where it goes and how much it costs (with a fictitious tariff).
ener.flujo_ayuda: The thickness and speed of each flow depend on the power. The photovoltaic system does not go through the meter: it enters the plant behind it, so what the meter buys or sells is the difference between what the boards consume and what it generates. Click a piece of equipment to see its page.
ener.tarifa_dia: Period and price for each hour of {fecha} (the current hour is outlined).
ener.tarifa_ayuda: Fictitious prices and periods, for practice only. The more intense the colour, the more expensive the energy.
ener.importados: bought from the grid this shift
ener.reparto_ayuda: Power of each piece of equipment in the latest sample and its share of the total.
ener.tendencia_ayuda: What the meter buys (positive) or sells (negative), its 15-min average (0 until the first full quarter-hour closes) and the photovoltaic generation.
ener.datos: Where to get the energy data
ener.curva_ayuda: One file per day, like the one the distribution company provides (with ; and decimal comma):
ener.media_pendiente: The meter calculates it when each full quarter-hour closes; none has closed since the simulator started.
ener.barra_ayuda: Junction point inside the plant: it receives what passes through the meter and what the photovoltaic system generates, and the boards come out of it. Its value is what the boards consume.
ficha.tabla_ayuda: The last 30 samples; the most recent at the top.
dest.periodo_ayuda: Tariff period: P1 is the most expensive and P6 the cheapest
portada.como_provocar: To trigger one, open the page of a piece of equipment (PLC, robots, CNC, compressor or photovoltaic system).
